preamble: Replacement of the postalveolar affricate [tʃ] by the glottal fricative [h] removes all oral articulation, keeping only voiceless frication. The clear attested case is loanword adaptation in Māori, which lacks affricates and sibilants and substitutes h for English /tʃ/ (as it does for /s/ and /ʃ/). Historical cases often cited for this cell instead pass through a fricative stage (tʃ > ʃ > h, as in Terena) or start from a different affricate (Proto-Tupí-Guaraní *ts > Guaraní h), and belong in those cells instead.

examples.note: Both instances of /tʃ/ are rendered h; listed as a loanword in Te Aka Māori Dictionary.
